statement: The frequency response of a system is the quantitative measure of the magnitude and phase of the output as a function of input frequency. In linear systems, it completely describes the system with a one-to-one correspondence to the time-domain impulse response as its Fourier transform, and is equivalent to the Laplace transfer function when the real part $\sigma$ of the complex variable $s = \sigma + j\omega$ is zero.

symbols.meaning: complex variable of the transfer function, defined as s = \sigma + j\omega
real part of the transfer function complex variable s

properties.property: The frequency response completely describes a linear system and has a one-to-one correspondence with the impulse response.
properties.why: the frequency response is the Fourier transform of the time-domain impulse response

properties.property: The overall frequency response of cascaded systems is obtained by the multiplication of the individual stages' frequency responses.
properties.why: frequency-domain multiplication corresponds to time-domain convolution of individual impulse responses

properties.property: The frequency response is equivalent to the system transfer function evaluated on the imaginary axis ($s = j\omega$).
properties.why: the real part $\sigma$ of the complex variable $s = \sigma + j\omega$ in the Laplace transform is zero

properties.property: Mathematical analysis of systems is simplified by converting governing differential equations into algebraic equations.
properties.why: the frequency response characterizes system input-output behavior directly in the frequency domain

properties.property: Closed-loop system stability and stability margins can be assessed from the open-loop frequency response via Bode, Nyquist, or Nichols plots.
properties.why: the plots parametrically or rectilinearly graph magnitude and phase against frequency

assumptions.assumption: The system is linear or can be approximated as linear by neglecting second-order non-linear properties.
assumptions.breaks_when: The system exhibits non-negligible non-linear behavior.

assumptions.assumption: The real part $\sigma$ of the complex variable $s = \sigma + j\omega$ is zero.
assumptions.breaks_when: The system transfer function is evaluated off the imaginary axis in the complex $s$-plane.

assumptions.assumption: The system reaches steady-state at each frequency during stepped sinusoidal measurement.
assumptions.breaks_when: The frequency sweep is stepped too fast for the system to reach steady-state at each frequency point of interest.

failure_modes.signature: Frequency response containing a main lobe with multiple periodic sidelobes
failure_modes.cause: Discrete digital processes including sampling and windowing

failure_modes.mode: Transient measurement distortion during sinusoidal sweep
failure_modes.signature: Measured output magnitude and phase shift deviate from the true steady-state frequency response
failure_modes.cause: Frequency sweep rate is too fast to allow the system to reach steady-state at each test frequency

failure_modes.mode: Loss of phase information in noise-excited response measurement
failure_modes.signature: Magnitude spectrum is captured without phase response
failure_modes.cause: Using the power spectral density instead of the cross-spectral density between input and output signals
